title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 14. Absorption in Balabhadra
html:
The Lord takes on the mood of Balarama: He calls for honey-wine, dances as if drunk, sees Halayudha and displays His form; the devotees see Balarama's companions and His golden club

Verse 1

अथ प्रभाते विमले द्युनाथे
स्मरन्मुनिब्राह्मणसज्जनान्बहून्।
स पाठयन्दैवतगौरचन्द्रो
बभूव नीलाम्बरभावभावितः॥१॥

atha prabhāte vimale dyunāthe
smaranmunibrāhmaṇasajjanānbahūn|
sa pāṭhayandaivatagauracandro
babhūva nīlāmbarabhāvabhāvitaḥ||1||

atha — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; dyu-nathe — (when) the lord of the sky (the sun); smaran — remembering; muni-brahmana-sat-janan — sages, brahmanas and saintly people; bahun — many; sah — He; pathayan — teaching (pupils); daivata-gaurachandrah — the divine Gaurachandra; babhuva — became; nila-ambara-bhava-bhavitah — imbued with the mood of Nilambara (the Blue-clad, Balarama).

1One morning at dawn, when the sun shone clear in the sky, the divine Gaurachandra, while teaching His pupils and remembering many sages, brahmanas and saintly people, became imbued with the mood of Nilambara1.

Verse 2

स हासयन्देहि मधूनि साम्प्रतं
त्वतीव तं मेघसमं स्वनं पुनः।
शुश्राव तस्मिन्समये हलायुधं
नीलाम्बरं श्वेतमहीधरं प्रभुम्॥२॥

sa hāsayandehi madhūni sāmprataṁ
tvatīva taṁ meghasamaṁ svanaṁ punaḥ|
śuśrāva tasminsamaye halāyudhaṁ
nīlāmbaraṁ śvetamahīdharaṁ prabhum||2||

sah — He; hasayan — making (all) laugh; dehi — give; madhuni — honey; sampratam — now; tu — and; ativa — exceedingly; tam — that; megha-samam — like a thundercloud; svanam — sound; punah — again; shushrava — heard; tasmin samaye — at that moment; halayudham — Halayudha (the Plough-armed); nila-ambaram — blue-clad; shveta-mahidharam — a white mountain; prabhum — the Lord.

2Making everyone laugh, He cried, "Give Me honey now!" — and then again He heard that deep sound, like the roar of a thundercloud: at that moment He heard Halayudha, the blue-clad Lord, like a white mountain;

Verse 3

सौनन्दपाणिं वरपद्मलोचनं
दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं हृष्टमनाः प्रहर्षयन्।
लोकान्ननर्ताखिललोकपालकः
स्वयं हरिस्तैर्मुनिभिः सुवेशधृक्॥३॥

saunandapāṇiṁ varapadmalocanaṁ
dṛṣṭvādbhutaṁ hṛṣṭamanāḥ praharṣayan|
lokānnanartākhilalokapālakaḥ
svayaṁ haristairmunibhiḥ suveśadhṛk||3||

saunanda-panim — with Saunanda in hand; vara-padma-lochanam — with beautiful lotus eyes; drishtva — seeing; adbhutam — the wondrous one; hrishta-manah — glad at heart; praharshayan — delighting; lokan — people; nanarta — danced; akhila-loka-palakah — the protector of all worlds; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; taih — with those; munibhih — sages; su-vesha-dhrik — in beautiful attire.

3and, seeing that wondrous Lord with Saunanda2 in His hand and beautiful lotus eyes, Hari, the protector of all worlds, in splendid attire, glad at heart and gladdening the people, began to dance together with those sages.

Verse 4

विप्रैरुपेतो हरिनामगायनै-
र्हृष्टोऽगमद्वैद्यमुरारिवेश्मनि।
तत्रावदद्देहि सुधां मधूत्कटां
प्राचीदिवानाथ इवातिलोहितः॥४॥

viprairupeto harināmagāyanai-
rhṛṣṭo'gamadvaidyamurāriveśmani|
tatrāvadaddehi sudhāṁ madhūtkaṭāṁ
prācīdivānātha ivātilohitaḥ||4||

vipraih — by brahmanas; upetah — accompanied; hari-nama-gayanaih — singing the name of Hari; hrishtah — joyful; agamat — went; vaidya-murari-veshmani — to the house of Murari the physician; tatra — there; avadat — said; dehi — give; sudham — nectar; madhu-utkatam — strong with honey; prachi-diva-nathah — the eastern sun; iva — like; ati-lohitah — deep red.

4Joyful, accompanied by brahmanas singing the name of Hari, He went to the house of Murari the physician, and there, as red as the sun in the east, He said: "Give Me nectar strong with honey!"

Verse 5

जिष्णुः स्वयं तोयसुपूर्णभाजनं
हस्तेन धृत्वापिबदम्बु पावनम्।
ननर्त मत्तोऽतिहसन्लुठन्क्षितौ
तदास्तुवंस्ते हलिनं द्विजोत्तमाः॥५॥

jiṣṇuḥ svayaṁ toyasupūrṇabhājanaṁ
hastena dhṛtvāpibadambu pāvanam|
nanarta matto'tihasanluṭhankṣitau
tadāstuvaṁste halinaṁ dvijottamāḥ||5||

jishnuh — the Victorious; svayam — Himself; toya-su-purna-bhajanam — a vessel full of water; hastena — with His hand; dhritva — holding; apibat — drank; ambu — the water; pavanam — purifying; nanarta — danced; mattah — intoxicated; ati-hasan — laughing loudly; luthan — rolling; kshitau — on the ground; tada — then; astuvan — praised; te — those; halinam — the Plough-bearer; dvija-uttamah — best of the twice-born.

5The Victorious One Himself took in His hand a vessel full of water and drank the purifying water; then, as if drunk, He danced, laughed aloud and rolled on the ground, while the best of the brahmanas praised Him as the Plough-bearer.

Verse 6

पेतुः पृथिव्यां चरणाम्बुजद्वये
मुमोद चातीव मुहुर्मुहुर्जनः।
एवं स देवो बलदेवलीलया
ननर्त चोवाच च सामनिस्वनः॥६॥

petuḥ pṛthivyāṁ caraṇāmbujadvaye
mumoda cātīva muhurmuhurjanaḥ|
evaṁ sa devo baladevalīlayā
nanarta covāca ca sāmanisvanaḥ||6||

petuh — fell; prithivyam — on the ground; charana-ambuja-dvaye — at the two lotus feet; mumoda — rejoiced; cha — and; ativa — exceedingly; muhuh-muhuh — again and again; janah — the people; evam — thus; sah — He; devah — the Lord; baladeva-lilaya — in the play of Baladeva; nanarta — danced; cha — and; uvacha — spoke; cha — and; sama-nisvanah — in a gentle voice.

6People fell to the ground at His lotus feet and rejoiced exceedingly, again and again. Thus the Lord, playing the part of Baladeva, danced and spoke in a gentle voice:

Verse 7

नाहं स कृष्णो वचसा सुखी भवे-
द्यो मे प्रयच्छन्तु सुपेयमद्भुतम्।
मल्लोऽयमित्यङ्गुलिना द्विजैकं
क्षिपन्सुदूरे प्राहिणोत्पृथिव्याम्॥७॥

nāhaṁ sa kṛṣṇo vacasā sukhī bhave-
dyo me prayacchantu supeyamadbhutam|
mallo'yamityaṅgulinā dvijaikaṁ
kṣipansudūre prāhiṇotpṛthivyām||7||

na — not; aham — I; sah — that; krishnah — Krishna; vachasa — with words; sukhi — content; bhavet — would be; yah — who; me — to Me; prayachchhantu — let them give; su-peyam — a fine drink; adbhutam — wondrous; mallah — a wrestler; ayam — this; iti — saying; angulina — with a finger; dvija-ekam — one brahmana; kshipan — flinging; su-dure — far away; prahinot — hurled; prithivyam — onto the ground.

7"I am not that Krishna who is content with words — let them bring Me a fine and wondrous drink!" And saying, "This one is a wrestler!", with a single finger He flung a brahmana far away onto the ground.

Verse 8

पपात सोऽप्यागतसाध्वसोऽभू-
देवं विजह्रे भगवान्स्वलीलया।
प्रातः समारभ्य दिवावसानं
यावत्स देवो बलदेवलीलया॥८॥

papāta so'pyāgatasādhvaso'bhū-
devaṁ vijahre bhagavānsvalīlayā|
prātaḥ samārabhya divāvasānaṁ
yāvatsa devo baladevalīlayā||8||

papata — fell; sah — he; api — and; agata-sadhvasah — seized with fear; abhut — became; evam — thus; vijahre — sported; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sva-lilaya — in His own play; pratah — from morning; samarabhya — beginning; diva-avasanam — the day's end; yavat — until; sah — He; devah — the Lord; baladeva-lilaya — in the play of Baladeva.

8The man fell and was terrified. So Bhagavan sported in His play: from early morning till the day's end the Lord, playing the part of Baladeva,

Verse 9

क्रीडां विधत्तेऽद्भुतरूपवेशः
स्वयं कृतस्नानविधिर्ययौ गृहम्।
भुङ्क्ते स्ववर्गैः परिवेष्टितः स्वयं
श्रीगौरचन्द्रो जगतां पतिः प्रभुः॥९॥

krīḍāṁ vidhatte'dbhutarūpaveśaḥ
svayaṁ kṛtasnānavidhiryayau gṛham|
bhuṅkte svavargaiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ svayaṁ
śrīgauracandro jagatāṁ patiḥ prabhuḥ||9||

kridam — play; vidhatte — performs; adbhuta-rupa-veshah — in wondrous form and attire; svayam — Himself; krita-snana-vidhih — having performed His bath; yayau — went; griham — home; bhunkte — eats; sva-vargaih — by His own; pariveshtitah — surrounded; svayam — Himself; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; jagatam — of the worlds; patih — master; prabhuh — the Lord.

9frolicked in wondrous form and attire; then, having bathed, He went home and ate surrounded by His own — Sri Gaurachandra Himself, the master of the worlds, the Lord.

Verse 10

अथापरेऽह्नि परितप्तदेहो
मुहुर्मुहुर्मोहमवाप देवः।
स्मरन्वने तं परिकीर्णमूर्धज-
स्तदा द्विजास्तं सलिलैरसिञ्चयन्॥१०॥

athāpare'hni paritaptadeho
muhurmuhurmohamavāpa devaḥ|
smaranvane taṁ parikīrṇamūrdhaja-
stadā dvijāstaṁ salilairasiñcayan||10||

atha — then; apare ahni — on another day; paritapta-dehah — His body burning; muhuh-muhuh — again and again; moham — a swoon; avapa — fell into; devah — the Lord; smaran — remembering; vane — in the forest; tam — Him (Balarama); parikirna-murdhajah — His hair dishevelled; tada — then; dvijah — the brahmanas; tam — Him; salilaih — with water; asinchayan — sprinkled.

10On another day the Lord's body burned, and again and again He fell into a swoon, remembering Him — Balarama — in the forest; His hair was dishevelled, and the brahmanas sprinkled Him with water.

Verse 11

गदाधरं सम्प्रति लब्धसंज्ञः
प्रोवाच वैकल्यगिरा स्वयं प्रभुः।
समानयासाद्य समस्तबन्धू-
न्सद्वैष्णवांस्तान्प्रतिलोकयामि॥११॥

gadādharaṁ samprati labdhasaṁjñaḥ
provāca vaikalyagirā svayaṁ prabhuḥ|
samānayāsādya samastabandhū-
nsadvaiṣṇavāṁstānpratilokayāmi||11||

gadadharam — to Gadadhara; samprati — now; labdha-sanjnah — having regained consciousness; provacha — said; vaikalya-gira — in a faltering voice; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord; samanaya — bring; asadya — finding; samasta-bandhun — all the friends; sat-vaishnavan — the true Vaishnavas; tan — those; pratilokayami — I would look upon.

11Coming to Himself, the Lord said to Gadadhara in a faltering voice: "Find all our friends and bring them here — I want to look upon those true Vaishnavas."

Verse 12

तदाज्ञया ते मुदिताः समागता
आचार्यरत्नप्रमुखा महत्तमाः।
दृष्ट्वा हरिं विह्वलितं सगद्गद-
स्वरं विमूढा इव ते भृशार्दिताः॥१२॥

tadājñayā te muditāḥ samāgatā
ācāryaratnapramukhā mahattamāḥ|
dṛṣṭvā hariṁ vihvalitaṁ sagadgada-
svaraṁ vimūḍhā iva te bhṛśārditāḥ||12||

tat-ajnaya — at His command; te — they; muditah — gladly; samagatah — assembled; acharyaratna-pramukhah — headed by Acharyaratna; mahat-tamah — the greatest souls; drishtva — seeing; harim — Hari; vihvalitam — overwhelmed; sa-gadgada-svaram — His voice faltering; vimudhah — bewildered; iva — as if; te — they; bhrisha-arditah — sorely distressed.

12At His command the greatest souls, headed by Acharyaratna3, gladly assembled. Seeing Hari overwhelmed, His voice breaking, they were bewildered and sorely distressed,

Verse 13

बभूवुरूचुश्च किमत्र कारणं
वदस्व तात स्वयमेव साम्प्रतम्।
श्रुत्वावदत्तान्नु हरिः सुविह्वलो
दृष्टो मया श्वेतगिरिर्हलायुधः॥१३॥

babhūvurūcuśca kimatra kāraṇaṁ
vadasva tāta svayameva sāmpratam|
śrutvāvadattānnu hariḥ suvihvalo
dṛṣṭo mayā śvetagirirhalāyudhaḥ||13||

babhuvuh — became; uchuh — said; cha — and; kim — what; atra — here; karanam — the cause; vadasva — tell; tata — dear one; svayam eva — Yourself; sampratam — now; shrutva — hearing; avadat — said; tan — to them; nu — then; harih — Hari; su-vihvalah — deeply overwhelmed; drishtah — has been seen; maya — by Me; shveta-girih — the white mountain; halayudhah — Halayudha.

13and said: "Dear Lord, tell us Yourself: what is the cause?" Hearing this, Hari, deeply shaken, answered them: "I have seen Halayudha, like a white mountain,

Verse 14

सुवर्णसौनन्दकरः सहस्रगु-
र्यथा प्रभाते वरहेमभूषणः।
श्रुत्वा तदा श्रीयुतचन्द्रशेखरा-
चार्योऽथ तं प्राह वदस्व तत्प्रभो॥१४॥

suvarṇasaunandakaraḥ sahasragu-
ryathā prabhāte varahemabhūṣaṇaḥ|
śrutvā tadā śrīyutacandraśekharā-
cāryo'tha taṁ prāha vadasva tatprabho||14||

suvarna-saunanda-karah — with the golden Saunanda in hand; sahasra-guh — the thousand-rayed (sun); yatha — like; prabhate — at dawn; vara-hema-bhushanah — adorned with the finest gold; shrutva — hearing; tada — then; shri-yuta-chandrashekhara-acharyah — the venerable Chandrashekhara Acharya; atha — then; tam — to Him; praha — said; vadasva — tell; tat — of that; prabho — O Lord.

14the golden Saunanda in His hand, shining like the thousand-rayed sun at dawn, adorned with the finest gold." Hearing this, the venerable Chandrashekhara Acharya said to Him: "Lord, tell us of the One

Verse 15

दृष्टस्त्वया यः सहसा तदा हरि-
स्तत्रैव गत्वा हलिनं ददर्श।
ततस्तदावेशतया पुनर्विभु-
र्ननर्त तद्वेशधरो मुदान्वितः॥१५॥

dṛṣṭastvayā yaḥ sahasā tadā hari-
statraiva gatvā halinaṁ dadarśa|
tatastadāveśatayā punarvibhu-
rnanarta tadveśadharo mudānvitaḥ||15||

drishtah — seen; tvaya — by You; yah — who; sahasa — suddenly; tada — then; harih — Hari; tatra eva — right there; gatva — going; halinam — the Plough-bearer; dadarsha — saw; tatah — then; tat-aveshataya — through absorption in Him; punah — again; vibhuh — the Almighty; nanarta — danced; tat-vesha-dharah — wearing His attire; muda-anvitah — joyful.

15whom You have seen." And at once Hari, as if gone there, beheld the Plough-bearer. And again the Almighty, wholly absorbed in Him, joyfully danced in His attire.

Verse 16

हृष्टो हरिः कौतुकनृत्यजल्पितै-
रानन्दितात्मा करभङ्गसङ्गतैः।
सद्वैष्णवैः पुण्यमहीधरोर्जितैः
क्रान्तैर्विधुः स्वर्गसुखं पदक्रमैः॥१६॥

hṛṣṭo hariḥ kautukanṛtyajalpitai-
rānanditātmā karabhaṅgasaṅgataiḥ|
sadvaiṣṇavaiḥ puṇyamahīdharorjitaiḥ
krāntairvidhuḥ svargasukhaṁ padakramaiḥ||16||

hrishtah — joyful; harih — Hari; kautuka-nritya-jalpitaih — by playful dances and talk; anandita-atma — His heart delighted; kara-bhanga-sangataih — accompanied by gestures of the hands; sat-vaishnavaih — by the true Vaishnavas; punya-mahidhara-urjitaih — mighty as holy mountains; krantaih — surpassing; vidhuh — the moon; svarga-sukham — the joy of heaven; pada-kramaih — with their steps.

16Hari rejoiced like the moon, His heart delighted by the true Vaishnavas — by their playful dancing and banter, the gestures of their hands, their strength like that of holy mountains, and their steps surpassing the bliss of heaven.

Verse 17

एवं दिनान्तं स निनाय यज्ञभु-
ग्यज्ञैः सुसङ्कीर्तनकैर्जगद्धितैः।
ततोऽपराह्णे पुनरेव देवे
नृत्योन्मुखे वारुणिदिव्यगन्धैः॥१७॥

evaṁ dināntaṁ sa nināya yajñabhu-
gyajñaiḥ susaṅkīrtanakairjagaddhitaiḥ|
tato'parāhṇe punareva deve
nṛtyonmukhe vāruṇidivyagandhaiḥ||17||

evam — thus; dina-antam — till the day's end; sah — He; ninaya — spent (the time); yajna-bhuk — the Enjoyer of sacrifices; yajnaih — with sacrifices; su-sankirtanakaih — of beautiful sankirtana; jagat-hitaih — beneficial to the world; tatah — then; aparahne — in the afternoon; punah eva — once again; deve — (when) the Lord; nritya-unmukhe — was about to dance; varuni-divya-gandhaih — with the divine fragrance of varuni.

17Thus the Enjoyer of sacrifices spent that day until evening in the sacrifice of beautiful sankirtana, which brings good to the world. Later, in the afternoon, when the Lord was once more about to dance, the divine fragrance of varuni

Verse 18

अपूरि सर्वाणि दिशां मुखानि
तदा समाघ्राय जना ननन्दुः।
श्रीरामनामा द्विजवर्यसत्तमो-
ऽपश्यत्तदा तत्र समागतान्बहून्॥१८॥

apūri sarvāṇi diśāṁ mukhāni
tadā samāghrāya janā nananduḥ|
śrīrāmanāmā dvijavaryasattamo-
'paśyattadā tatra samāgatānbahūn||18||

apuri — were filled; sarvani — all; disham — of the directions; mukhani — the faces; tada — then; samaghraya — inhaling (it); janah — the people; nananduh — rejoiced; shri-rama-nama — named Sri Rama; dvija-varya-sattamah — the best of excellent brahmanas; apashyat — saw; tada — then; tatra — there; samagatan — arrived; bahun — many.

18filled every quarter, and the people, breathing it in, rejoiced. Then the best of excellent brahmanas, named Sri Rama, saw that a multitude of beings had come there:

Verse 19

कर्णैकपद्मान्कमलायतेक्षणा-
ञ्छ्रोत्रैकविन्यस्तसुकुण्डलार्चिषा।
विद्योतमानान्सितवस्त्रमस्तका-
ञ्छ्रुत्वा ततोऽन्ये ननृतुः प्रहर्षिताः॥१९॥

karṇaikapadmānkamalāyatekṣaṇā-
ñchrotraikavinyastasukuṇḍalārciṣā|
vidyotamānānsitavastramastakā-
ñchrutvā tato'nye nanṛtuḥ praharṣitāḥ||19||

karna-eka-padman — with a lotus at one ear; kamala-ayata-ikshanan — with eyes wide as lotuses; shrotra-eka-vinyasta-su-kundala-archisha — with the radiance of a fine earring set in one ear; vidyotamanan — shining; sita-vastra-mastakan — their heads in white cloth; shrutva — hearing (of it); tatah — then; anye — others; nanrituh — danced; praharshitah — rejoicing.

19each had a lotus at one ear and eyes wide as lotuses; they shone with the radiance of a fine earring set in the other ear, and their heads were bound with white cloth4. Hearing of this, the others danced in delight.

Verse 20

तत्रैव कश्चिद्वनमालिनामा
पश्यत्यलं काञ्चननिर्मितं क्षितौ।
सौनन्दनं सूर्यकरप्रकाशकं
संहृष्टरोमाश्रुभिरार्द्रविग्रहः॥२०॥

tatraiva kaścidvanamālināmā
paśyatyalaṁ kāñcananirmitaṁ kṣitau|
saunandanaṁ sūryakaraprakāśakaṁ

✦

Notes

  1. Nilambara ("the Blue-clad"), Halayudha ("He whose weapon is the plough"), the Plough-bearer, Balabhadra and Baladeva are names of Balarama, Krishna's elder brother. Balarama is fond of the intoxicating drink varuni, hence the demand for honey. Balarama's varuni is not worldly wine but a divine drink, an image of His rapture in love (cf. 2.9, note 4); the Lord Himself drinks only pure water in this pastime (v. 5).
  2. Saunanda is Balarama's club (mace).
  3. Acharyaratna is Chandrashekhara Acharya.
  4. This is the appearance of Balarama and His companions: an earring in one ear and a lotus at the other.
